definition: The data a GPU must read from memory to generate one token: roughly the model's weights (read once per decode step and shared by the batch) plus each user's KV cache. Dividing memory bandwidth by it gives the decode ceiling.

The most tokens per second memory bandwidth can feed during decode: bandwidth divided by bytes per token. A 70B-parameter FP8 model is capped at about 48 tokens/s per stream on an H100 and about 274 on Rubin.
A vertical copper wire etched through a thinned silicon die so that stacked dies can pass data, power and ground straight up and down. Thousands of TSVs per die make HBM stacks possible.
A tiny solder joint, tens of micrometres across, that connects one stacked die to the next or a die to an interposer. HBM stacks use thousands per layer.
Joining two dies directly copper-to-copper and oxide-to-oxide, with no solder bumps. It allows denser, thinner and cooler stacks and is being explored for 16-high HBM4E and beyond.
How many DRAM dies are stacked in one HBM stack (8-, 12- or 16-high). Height times die density sets capacity: twelve 24 Gb dies give 36 GB, sixteen 32 Gb dies give 64 GB.
TSMC's original CoWoS variant, which places dies on one monolithic silicon interposer of up to about 3.3 times the reticle area. Used for A100, H100 and H200.
A TSMC CoWoS variant whose interposer is made only of organic redistribution layers, with no silicon. Cheaper and more flexible but with coarser wiring than CoWoS-S or CoWoS-L.
A small piece of silicon with very fine wiring, embedded under the edges of neighbouring dies in a CoWoS-L package, so that silicon is used only where dense connections are needed.

Thin layers of metal wiring built on top of an organic or silicon base to route signals between dies and to the package's connections; coarser than wiring inside a chip but far finer than a circuit board.
Intel's 3D packaging technology that stacks logic dies face to face. Offered with EMIB as an alternative to TSMC's packaging for multi-die AI chips.
Building advanced packages on large rectangular panels instead of round 300 mm wafers. Rectangles waste less edge area when each package spans several reticles, but panels warp more.
A company that sells servers under its own brand, often built partly by ODMs, and adds sales, service and financing; in AI servers, for example Dell, HPE and Supermicro.

Industry shorthand for how complete a server build is: L6 is a populated board or module, L10 a complete tested server or tray, and L11 a whole rack with networking, power and cooling, validated as one unit.
NVIDIA's BlueField-4-based storage tier, launched at CES 2026, that holds and shares KV-cache blocks across inference nodes so long conversations can be reloaded instead of recomputed.

An NVIDIA GPU announced in September 2025 for the prefill (context) phase of inference, with 128 GB of GDDR7 instead of HBM. It was absent from the March 2026 roadmap; a revival with HBM4 is reported but unconfirmed.
